title: For Ever Blessed Be the Lord
description: For Ever Blessed Be the Lord in Tonic Solfa to CAITHNESS, doh is D: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 3 verses and a piano.
about: Isaac Watts wrote these words for The Psalms of David Imitated in the Language of the New Testament (1719): Psalm 144, part 1, headed “Assistance and victory in the spiritual warfare”.
Watts' psalms were printed without tunes and sung to any tune of their metre, Common Metre (8.6.8.6). This page sets the words to CAITHNESS; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: For ev-er bless-ed be the Lord, My Sa-viour and my shield; He sends his Spir-it with his word To arm me for the field.

lines: For ever blessed be the Lord,
He sends his Spirit with his word
To arm me for the field.
When sin and hell their force unite,
He makes my soul his care,
Instructs me to the heavenly fight,
And guards me thro' the war.
A friend and helper so divine
He makes the glorious victory mine,
And his shall be the praise.

source: Isaac Watts, The Psalms of David Imitated (1719)
licence: Public domain: Isaac Watts died in 1748.
credits: Words by Isaac Watts (1674–1748), public domain; set to CAITHNESS by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
